description: Issue #839 (maintainer ruling #833 rule 3, "nothing shadows"): `define forward … print 1 … end` then `print fd`. The runtime phase-1 registration guard (`spec/execution-model.md:82-89`) raises `ol-reserved-word` (`spec/error-model.md:125`) at the declaration, so the procedure never runs and the event stream is empty. Since issue #815 the check also sees the `print fd` on the last line and reports its own faults there, so the empty event stream — not the absence of a reporter-position finding — is what evidences the halt. Re-legalising `define forward` reddens this and leads the next reader to #787. The evaluator-level invariant is carried in `packages/runtime/src/heritage-alias-chokepoint.test.mjs`. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists, but it runs only under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — NOT in this fixture, which is checked — and when it does run it is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why the runtime's copy never appears beside the check's. So nothing here observes that copy, and reading this fixture as evidence for it would be a mistake: measured, a runtime guard can be deleted outright with the whole conformance corpus still green, because the surviving report is the check's either way. What the runtime copy uniquely contributes is that the run STOPS at the fault, which is written in the event stream rather than in the diagnostics and is pinned by `packages/runtime/src/runtime-guards-halt.test.mjs`. The other findings recorded here are independent faults in the same program, each reported once.
